reason: Fix one state and use only its point mass μ. Define ν_n=n^{-1}∑_{k=0}^{n−1}μP^k. The vectors lie in the closed finite simplex. Apply the published real Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem successively to finitely many coordinates, retaining nested subsequences, to get ν_{n_j}→π. Finite sums preserve nonnegativity and mass one. The exact telescoping identity ν_nP−ν_n=(μP^n−μ)/n tends to zero coordinatewise, so πP=π. No arbitrary choice or path law is used.
